findings.description: The deploy user's inline policy grants ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, and cloudwatch:* on Resource "*", giving full administrative control of compute, storage, serverless, and monitoring services. This breaks least privilege, allows full data exfiltration/overwrite of every S3 object, and lets the user modify or delete other workloads; combined with the EC2 wildcard it also permits privilege escalation via instance-user-data or existing-role manipulation.

A static, non-rotating IAM access key is created for the deploy user. Long-lived access keys paired with the wildcard policy above are the classic credential-leak vector, since anyone obtaining the key gains the full ec2:*/s3:*/lambda:*/cloudwatch:* privileges without MFA or expiry.

findings.issue_category: secret emitted to output and state
findings.description: This output surfaces the IAM access key secret material from aws_iam_access_key.svc_deploy_key via Terraform output, persisting the credential in plaintext in the state file and any consumer of the output (CI logs, remote state readers). This exposes the secret key beyond the trust boundary of whoever manages the key.
